name: Saint Casimir
history: A prince of Poland and Lithuania, son of King Casimir IV, who lived at the heart of a powerful court as quietly as a monk. He prayed through the night, gave freely to the poor, loved Our Lady and refused a royal marriage to remain chaste. He died of tuberculosis at twenty-five and is the patron of Lithuania.
life: Casimir was the second son of Casimir IV Jagiellon and Elizabeth of Austria, and was taught by the historian Jan Długosz. In 1471, at thirteen, his father sent him with an army to take the crown of Hungary, offered by nobles opposed to King Matthias Corvinus. The venture failed and Casimir came home, and he seems never to have wanted a throne again. For a time he governed Poland while his father was in Lithuania, and he was known for fairness and for his care of the poor. He slept little, often praying at church doors before they opened, and was said to wear a hair shirt beneath his fine clothes. He declined a proposed marriage to a daughter of the Emperor. He died at Grodno on 4 March 1484 and was buried in Vilnius Cathedral, by tradition with a copy of the Marian hymn Omni die dic Mariae, which he loved.
prayerTo: Saint Casimir, you lived among wealth and power and kept your heart for God alone. Teach me to use what I have for the poor, to guard my purity, and to love the Mother of God with a simple and faithful love. Pray for Lithuania and Poland, and for all who carry responsibility for others. Amen.
penance: Casimir gave his princely income to the poor. Give today what you would have spent on a treat, and pray one Hail Mary for each person you pass who looks in need.
meditation: He had every comfort a court could give and chose to kneel at the church door before dawn. What comfort keeps you from prayer?
